items.text: Support your needy relatives, so that they do not become a charge on the town.
items.citation: Warning Out in New England, Chapter III
items.quote: unless relatives be of sufficient ability to do so

items.text: Entertain a brother newly arrived from England, securing the town from any damage during his residence.
items.citation: Warning Out in New England, 1656-1817, Chapter II.
items.quote: entertaine his brother as is aboue expressed

items.text: Give shelter to a daughter in winter; do not turn her out of doors, even when the town requires it.
items.citation: Warning Out in New England, 1656-1817, Chapter II.
items.quote: she was their daughter and Could not turn her out of doars this winter time

items.text: Provide for his wife and take her into his own home, so that she does not remain a charge on her father.
items.citation: Warning Out in New England, 1656-1817, Chapter II.
items.quote: being marryed to Thomas Chub... is not p'uided for by her said husband, nor taken home to him

items.text: Betake herself to her husband, leaving her father's house and dwelling with him.
items.citation: Warning Out in New England, 1656-1817, Chapter II.
items.quote: doe speedily... betake herself to her said husband

items.text: Be a help to his father and mother in their need.
items.citation: Warning Out in New England, 1656-1817, Chapter II.
items.quote: he might be an help to his father and mother

items.text: Be chargeable for his support if he is lamed or any way unserviceable made in work during the time for which he is hired, so the town may be free from such charges.
items.citation: Warning Out in New England, 1656-1817, Chapter V
items.quote: all persons who should hire any servant should be chargeable for his support 'if it happened that he should be lamed or any way unserviceable made in work during the time for which he was hired, so the town may be free from such charges.'

items.text: Support your household so that they do not become a burden on the town.
items.citation: Warning Out in New England, 1656-1817, Chapter IV.
items.quote: have supported him or herself, and his or her family

items.text: Maintain him if he falls sick or lame during his indenture or covenant.
items.citation: Warning Out in New England, Ch. V
items.quote: if such servant shal fal sick, or lame. He shal be maintained by his Master during the date of his indenture, or coven't

items.text: Support yourself and your family, so that you do not become chargeable to the town.
items.citation: Warning Out in New England, Chapter IV, Section 4
items.quote: shall have supported him or herself, and his or her Family

items.text: Relieve your needy kinsman, as the law holds you liable for his support.
items.citation: Warning Out in New England, Chapter IV, Section 10
items.quote: unless the Person so entertained hath Relations who by Law are liable for his Support

items.text: Receive your son-in-law and his family into your house when they are in poor circumstances.
items.citation: Warning Out in New England, 1656-1817, Chapter III.
items.quote: she took into her house as inmates her sonin-law, Nathaniel Whittemore, with his wife and child, under poor circumstances

items.text: When ordered to depart, take your children with you; do not leave them behind.
items.citation: Warning Out in New England, Chapter VI
items.quote: depart the Limits thereof, With their Children And others under their care

items.text: Relieve your child if he is poor and you are able, as the justices of the peace shall assess.
items.citation: Warning Out in New England, Chapter V
items.quote: unless the relations of such poor impotent persons in the line of father, or grand-father, mother, or grand-mother, children, or grandchildren be of sufficient ability; then such relations respectively shall relieve such poor person
